title: good first issue: add a CONTRIBUTING section on "how to run the cross-language conformance tests"
body:
## What

Add a section to `CONTRIBUTING.md` titled "Running the cross-language conformance tests" that explains:

1. Where the shared conformance vectors live (`conformance/`)
2. How to run the Python conformance tests (`pytest tests/test_canonical.py`)
3. How to run the Rust conformance tests (`cargo test --manifest-path alethech-rs/Cargo.toml`)
4. How to run the TypeScript conformance tests (`cd alethech-ts && npm test`)
5. Why all three implementations must agree (the cross-language signature contract)

## Why

Right now, a new contributor who wants to verify their change doesn't break cross-language compatibility has to read the source of all three SDKs to figure out where the test entry points are. CONTRIBUTING.md exists but doesn't cover this.

The cross-language contract is the load-bearing property of the whole protocol — if a Python-signed commit stops verifying in TypeScript, the protocol is broken. So contributors need to know how to check this.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New section in `CONTRIBUTING.md` titled "Running the cross-language conformance tests"
- [ ] Lists the exact commands for all three languages
- [ ] Explains what "pass" means (all three suites green)
- [ ] Explains what to do if one suite fails but others pass (that's a bug — open an issue)
- [ ] Links to the conformance vectors directory and explains what each vector tests
- [ ] No more than 80 lines total (this is a how-to, not an essay)

## Difficulty

Beginner-friendly. No code changes — just documentation. You'll need to install the three SDKs locally to verify the commands work, but installation is one command each (`pip install -e .`, `cargo build`, `npm install`).

## What you'll learn

- How the three SDKs are structured
- Where the conformance vectors live and what they test
- Why cross-language parity is the protocol's most important property

## Mentoring

I'll review PRs within 24 hours. If you find that the documented commands don't work on your machine, that's a bug — open an issue separately and we'll fix the underlying problem.
